opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by funding the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for a decade; first five years' funding of £3,500 claimable in year 1, plus additional £3,500 in year 6

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funding over 10 years for long-term ecological studies, enabling existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, covering ecological restoration, habitat creation, alien species control and climate change.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Funding research on education methods within ecology to develop evidence informing teaching and learning practices, improving the student experience and promoting excellence in teaching.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals.
opportunities.summary: Funding interdisciplinary placements (secondments) of up to 12 months that immerse an ecologist in another professional world (another discipline, NGO, public sector, business) to develop interdisciplinary skills.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Funding for researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world.
opportunities.summary: Funding for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Funding for BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £500 is available for events in person; a maximum of £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher; work or study at a university or research institution; work in scientific areas within the ecology remit.
opportunities.summary: Grants to help PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to present their work at workshops and conferences.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; at least three years since last BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering travel, registration, food and accommodation costs.
